The frequency of genotypes for a given trait are given in the accompanying graph. Answer the following questions using this information:

Is this population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a genotype frequency table, with the three columns labeled AA, Aa, and aa respectively; the corresponding frequencies are shown as AA = 36%, Aa = 45%, aa = ?%. Reasoning: The sum of the three genotype frequencies should be 100%, so aa = 100% - 36% - 45% = 19%. The observed frequencies are AA = 0.36, Aa = 0.45, aa = 0.19. Calculate allele frequencies from the observed frequencies: p = f(AA) + 0.5f(Aa) = 0.36 + 0.5(0.45) = 0.585; q = 1 - p = 0.415. If in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, the expected frequency of heterozygote Aa should be 2pq = 2(0.585)(0.415) ≈ 0.486, that is, 48.6%. This is not equal to the observed Aa = 45% in the figure, therefore this population does not conform to Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
